title: Cross-Site Scripting
brief: **Ticket:** a greeting page reflects your name straight into the HTML. A simulated admin bot visits pages. Land a script and steal what the bot leaks.
theory:
## Reflected XSS (OWASP A03)
The app puts your input into HTML without encoding, so `<script>` runs in the victim's browser — stealing cookies, acting as them.

**Fix:** contextual output encoding (`<` becomes `<`) plus a Content-Security-Policy.
worked_example:
``` $ curl "https://x/greet?name="

Hello

# runs in the victim's browser ```

investigation.intro: Send a script payload; the admin bot 'runs' it and leaks its cookie in a response header.
steps:
```bash
cd /workspaces/examto/ctf-lab
python3 -m venv .venv 2>/dev/null; . .venv/bin/activate 2>/dev/null; pip install -q -r requirements.txt
python3 target/run_target.py        # leave this running
```

In a second terminal, send a script payload and read the response headers:
```bash
curl -s -D - "http://127.0.0.1:5000/greet?name=<script>x</script>" -o /dev/null
```
Look for the `X-Admin-Cookie` header — its value is the flag.
hints: A <script> tag or onerror= triggers the bot.
Read the response headers, not the body (-D -).
The flag is in the X-Admin-Cookie header.

capture.task: **Capture the flag.** Land an XSS payload and submit the value of the `X-Admin-Cookie` header.
capture.hint: curl -D - with a <script> name, read X-Admin-Cookie
